body:
Follow-up to #41196

## Problem

Since #29976, the custom 'tabline' has a base highlight group `TabLineFill` that all `%#` highlights are automatically combined with. But the default C implementation still uses the `TabLine` and `TabLineSel` highlight groups uncombined, or rather effectively combined with `Normal`. Therefore, themes cannot depend on the base highlighting if they want to support both the default and custom tab lines.

## Solution

Automatically combine `TabLine` and `TabLineSel` with `TabLineFill` in the default C implementation.

## Notes

For each tab, the default 'tabline' uses either `TabLine` or `TabLineSel`, and combines that with `Title` for the window count, and `TabLine` is also reused for the close button and 'showcmd' on the right. The style of each tab can be overridden with `TabLine`, `TabLineSel`, and `Title` local to the focused window in the respective tab, for example:
```lua
local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("test")
vim.api.nvim_set_hl(ns, "TabLineSel", { fg = "red" })
vim.api.nvim_win_set_hl_ns(0, ns)
```
Theoretically, the base `TabLineFill` could also be taken from the window's namespace, but that would make it even harder to re-implement in lua if the C implementation should be replaced, since `win_redr_stl_expr` only supports a single base highlight for the whole expression.

There was also kind of a circular dependency: `TabLineFill` linked to `TabLine`, which "inherits" from `TabLineFill`. Since `TabLineFill` is the base highlight that all others depend on, I flipped that link.

Closes #41173

comment_regular_data.body:
> Since #29976, the custom 'tabline' has a base highlight group `TabLineFill` that all `%#` highlights are automatically combined with. But the default C implementation still uses the `TabLine` and `TabLineSel` highlight groups uncombined, or rather effectively combined with `Normal`. Therefore, themes cannot depend on the base highlighting if they want to support both the default and custom tab lines.

Can you please craft a *small* reproducible demonstration of the problem. I am having hard time figuring out the specifics of why switching the default definition of `TabLine` and `TabLineFill` is needed.

@echasnovski Absolutely. It is not really *needed*, but I think it's better that way. I have a more detailed explanation in the second commit message, but of course, I couldn't add images in there. For reference, the tabline is of course designed to look like the non-current status-line: Let's say, I want to customise only how inactive tabs look like, but not the rest of the tabline. My expectation is that I only have to configure `TabLine` to get the following: But unfortunately, since the base highlight group `TabLineFill` links to `TabLine`, this would also change the background of the whole tab line and potentially all other highlights that are combined with `TabLineFill`: The other way around, this is more expected: the link `TabLine -> TabLineFill` expresses that inactive tabs should look exactly like the tab line background, i.e. the only difference is that inactive tabs contain title text. Therefore, when I configure `TabLineFill`, I expect inactive tabs to adapt accordingly. Even without the link, I would expect a change to `TabLineFill` to affect inactive tabs, since `TabLine` is automatically combined with `TabLineFill`. I find the naming of these highlight groups a bit unfortunate from today's point of view. At first glance, it looks like `TabLine` would be the master/main/base, and both `TabLineFill` and `TabLineSel` somehow subordinate, just like the status line's base highlight is `StatusLine` and not `StatusLineFill`. The alphabetical order in `syntax.txt` and `highlight_group.c` reinforces that impression. Even the original `news.txt` entry of PR #29976 wrongly claims that tab line highlights are combined with `TabLine`. I suspect that this is how the current link `TabLineFill -> TabLine` came about. Correct me if I'm wrong, maybe I'm missing something. That said, that change it is definitely not needed to close the issue and the workaround for my example is also simple enough: if you want to customise only inactive tabs, configure `TabLine` and add `hi link TabLineFill StatusLineNC`.

> Let's say, I want to customise only how inactive tabs look like, but not the rest of the tabline. My expectation is that I only have to configure `TabLine` to get the following:

Well, this reasoning goes the other way also. What if after this PR one wants to customize only `TabLineFill`? Adjusting only it will also affect `TabLine`.

> I find the naming of these highlight groups a bit unfortunate from today's point of view. At first glance, it looks like `TabLine` would be the master/main/base, and both `TabLineFill` and `TabLineSel` somehow subordinate, just like the status line's base highlight is `StatusLine` and not `StatusLineFill`.

That was my impression as well. Do you (or @ribru17) happen to figure out was it always the case that `TabLineFill` was used as base highlight for tabline, or did it change after that PR?

If anything, the fact that `TabLineFill` is the "main" group that is used for combining with other groups indeed makes `TabLine` linking to `TabLineFill` more relevant.

> Well, this reasoning goes the other way also. What if after this PR one wants to customize only `TabLineFill`? Adjusting only it will also affect `TabLine`.

That is true, but I think that is more expected, at least in my intuition: the inactive tabs are "above" the base, and are configured to be "transparent" to let the base shine through. Therefore, changing the base style affects the inactive tabs. I think I didn't phrase it well enough, but that point was meant to be more about semantics and expectations than about optimising what leads to more or less work for users. But, of course, intuition can vary.

An alternative that takes advantage of the new base highlighting would be this:
```vim
hi link TabLineFill StatusLineNC
hi TabLine NONE
```
In other words: if `TabLine` should look like the base `TabLineFill`, just combine that base with *nothing*. Let me know if you prefer that, but in any case, the mere existence of that alternative suggests to me that `TabLineFill` should link to `StatusLineNC` directly.

> was it always the case that TabLineFill was used as base highlight for tabline, or did it change after that PR

It was always the case. The news entry contradicts the code changes. A simple mistake to make, since it is only natural to assume that if `StatusLine` is the base highlight of the status line, then `TabLine` should also be the base highlight of the tab line. The C code of the default tab line also defines `TabLineFill` as the *default* outside of the tabs, and therefore I think it was also chosen as the *default* for the custom tab line, even before the base-combining was introduced.

Here's a better phrasing: previously, in Vim, the following intuition is natural: there are different highlight groups for different parts of the tab line.

In Neovim, since #29976, my intuition changed: `TabLineFill` is not a *part*, but the *base* that is beneath everything else and can affect everything else through combination. If I change a highlight group like `TabLine` that is supposed to style only *part* of the tab line, I don't expect that to potentially affect everything else.

> An alternative that takes advantage of the new base highlighting would be this:
> 
> ```viml
> hi link TabLineFill StatusLineNC
> hi TabLine NONE
> ```
> 
> In other words: if `TabLine` should look like the base `TabLineFill`, just combine that base with _nothing_. Let me know if you prefer that, but in any case, the mere existence of that alternative suggests to me that `TabLineFill` should link to `StatusLineNC` directly.

No, thanks. Swapping `TabLine` with `TabLineFill` is just fine. One of the objectives for the default color scheme is to also serve as a reasonable default for semantically linked groups. I get that the effect might be similar, but here it makes more sense to me if they still get linked.

The `default link TabLine TabLineFill` and `default link TabLineFill StatusLineNC` is just fine. Although this is a *slightly* breaking change for the downstream groups, making `TabLineFill` the "main" group here does make more sense.

@echasnovski wonderful, thank you for your input! And thank you for the awesome default theme!

Since it's only *slightly* breaking, I won't add a news entry unless requested.

> Since it's only _slightly_ breaking, I won't add a news entry unless requested.

Sure, changes in default color scheme rarely (if ever) get to be part of the news.

The failing tests look relevant, though.

@echasnovski 

> The failing tests look relevant, though.

Indeed, just like your PR was a prerequisite for this one, equivalent changes are needed to the vim color scheme in order to fix the tests. They are of course needed anyway to fix the custom 'tabline'.

There are also some other test problems to fix. And after that is done, only 28 more bundled themes to go before I can press the publish button. Technically, #29976 broke those themes already, but my PR would break them much more if left unadapted.

> There are also some other test problems to fix. And after that is done, only 28 more bundled themes to go before I can press the publish button. Technically, #29976 broke those themes already, but my PR would break them much more if left unadapted.

If that's the case (i.e. this requires a lot of changes to the bundled color schemes), then this is a (serious) argument to not merge the changes from this PR. The bundled color schemes are generally ported from Vim as is. Having them differ will introduce problems when porting patches.

With this kind of churn and side effects this changes provides, I'd maybe reconsider if it is needed at all. Maybe if the same C code change is done in Vim (with bundled color schemes updated accordingly there), then the rest of the changes about the Neovim's default color scheme will be worth. But not sure if Vim will be interested in this kind of changes.

@echasnovski 

> But not sure if Vim will be interested in this kind of changes.

I see.. :(

But in light of the long-term goal of replacing old C implementations of 'statusline'-like options with 'statusline' expressions (+ in this case some lua), it seems important to harmonise the default and the custom tab line. So I think, the only other good alternative would be to make `Normal` the base highlight group of the tab line. Maybe, having a base is much less useful here anyway, compared to status line and winbar. The counter-intuitive fact that the base is not called `TabLine` would also not be a problem anymore.

I'll leave this as a draft until there is a consensus.
